And so for those of you who don't know, which might just be some residents, the Westchester Power Program is a community energy program. There are 27 municipalities across Westchester in the program currently, including five out of six of the municipalities in NYSIG territory, Lewisboro included. You all have been participating since 2016. And in the most recent contract, which began in 2019, you switched to the green supply. So that's really exciting. It's backed by 100% New York State hydropower. And we are going into our third contract beginning December 1st. So I've got a nice little short and sweet presentation for you all. We're gonna talk about the bid results and the new contract information. So again, there's 27 municipalities in the program. 24, including Lewisboro are in the green supply. And that makes up about 115,000 residents and small businesses across the county. This looks confusing at first, but I'll walk you through it. So the suppliers, we had four of them, which is up 100% from our last bid in which we only had two suppliers. We're able to bid against each other. And as you can see, drive the price downward. And we came in under our not to exceed price and secured a rate of 7.19 cents for the green power. So as you can see, again, we've got people outbidding each other, trying to get the rates as low as possible, but we did know, and you can see it at the end, that we wanted to come in under that 7.2. text: We've been discussing putting a cell tower in South Salem and in particular next to the salt dome. We had applied over two years ago to join a Northern Westchester group of towns which would come up with a master plan for constructing cell towers throughout Northern Westchester. In other words, Bedford, Lewisborough, North Salem, Mount Kisco, Pound Ridge, Somers, and Yorktown. Quite honestly, I and I think quite a lot of other supervisors had assumed that that had gone into a trash can somewhere in spite of our request and that nothing was ever going to happen. However, Kitley Covill, for which she should be much thanked revived this proposal, pushed it through the county and the county is funding this master plan for a fee of $190,170. It's not a cheap plan. It will be a four-month process for these towns. So it should be, I'd love to say it will be ready by February, but quite honestly, granted the way these things go, I think it will be more like March or April before it's complete and delivered. This sounds like a total gift and it is in terms of surveying this area of the county which has been much neglected for this and therefore has been subject to the individual telephone companies and people like Homeland Towers.
